final_answer: Approved: replace the broken single-pass deep-audit (deep:deep_failed) with a milestone-triggered, multi-agent ADVERSARIAL audit built on the bridge's own orchestration (driver agent-invoke + lib/parallel.ps1), following the operator-proven three-phase pattern — FIND (N parallel dimension-specialist finders, structured JSON output) → VERIFY (false-by-default skeptics that must cite file:line to refute; majority-refute discards) → SYNTHESIZE (dedup, severity-rank, idempotent auto-task creation in the backlog). The cheap nightly static-grep audit stays as the daily guard; the new adversarial audit is a separate, rare, on-demand/milestone-only mode. Agents are Claude CLI + Codex CLI ONLY (no raw API, no Gemini), mixing models and reasoning tiers for perspective diversity, using thin prompts + fat tools (codex -s read-only, claude -p --allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob --add-dir) so the CLI reads real code rather than receiving stdin-stuffed snippets. The single resource-allocation conflict (CONCURRENCY_FLOOR_20PLUS vs COST_CONTROL_BUDGET_DEPTH) is resolved per the user's hard requirement: the >=20 concurrent floor is honored as the default for milestone deep runs whenever >=20 units of work exist, and is NOT lowered to satisfy rate limits (429s are absorbed by refill-queue + cross-provider rebalancing + backoff). The budget profile does not throttle instantaneous width below 20 — it bounds the RUN's total size (total-agent cap, token ceiling, configurable depth = #dimensions / verifiers-per-finding / rounds) and the early-exit when FIND yields zero findings. Thus budget bounds how much total work and spend a run may incur; the floor governs how wide the live fan-out runs while work remains. Real parallelism is proven by live PID sampling recording peak_concurrency and a timeline in the report (assert peak>=20 when work is sufficient). Per-agent fault isolation ensures one timeout/crash/empty-reply never aborts a phase. Nothing gets built until the PROJECT_MAP+PLAN is written, architect-reviewed, and user-approved.

decisions.decision: ARCH_3PHASE_REPLACE_DEEPLLM — Adopt FIND → VERIFY → SYNTHESIZE adversarial architecture and retire the broken deep:deep_failed deep-LLM path.
decisions.rationale: Multi-proposal (A,C), judge total 0.83. The current deep-LLM pass is demonstrably broken (deep:deep_failed) and does a single un-verified pass; the proven operator pattern found 17 verified bugs. Swapping a known-broken component for a proven structure is the highest-impact, foundational bet and de-risks the entire system.
alternatives_considered: Patch/repair the existing deep:deep_failed subprocess/job layer in place
Keep single-pass finder dump and bolt on light scoring without an adversarial verify stage
decisions.risk: Low reversibility and high build cost; touches the core audit path. Mitigated by keeping the nightly static guard untouched and gating all build on the approved plan.
decisions.test: Confirm deep:deep_failed code path is removed/disabled and a run exhibits three distinct execution phases (FIND, VERIFY, SYNTHESIZE) with phase boundaries observable in logs/artifacts.

decisions.decision: AUDIT_MODES_SEPARATION — Two modes: existing cheap nightly static guard (unchanged) and a new milestone/on-demand adversarial deep audit, never triggered by the nightly cron.
decisions.rationale: Unanimous (A,B,C), judge 0.825. Correct operational split: keeps a cheap daily watchdog while ensuring the expensive 20+-agent run only fires on milestones (pre-training, post-major-pipeline-change, operator on-demand). Prevents the cron from accidentally launching costly deep runs.
alternatives_considered: Run the adversarial deep audit nightly
Replace the nightly static audit entirely with the deep audit
decisions.risk: Trigger wiring could accidentally bind deep mode to cron. Mitigated by an explicit trigger contract and a test asserting the nightly job invokes only the static path.
decisions.test: Verify the nightly static audit runs independently and the deep adversarial audit is reachable only via operator command or named milestone hooks — never by the nightly schedule.

decisions.decision: CONCURRENCY_FLOOR_20PLUS (MODIFIED — conflict resolution) — Maintain a hard floor of >=20 concurrent active agents during FIND and VERIFY whenever >=20 units of work exist, via a refill-queue worker pool that replaces the static maxParallelAgents cap. The floor is NOT lowered to satisfy rate limits; it relaxes only when fewer than 20 jobs remain outstanding. The budget profile bounds the RUN's total size (total-agent cap, token ceiling, depth), not its instantaneous width.
decisions.rationale: Unanimous mechanism (A,B,C); judge verdict 'modify' (0.68) flagged tension with budget/429 reality. The user's contract (msg 53853633) makes 20-concurrent a HARD, non-negotiable floor that overrides min(cores-2,N) and explicitly forbids dropping below 20 — cost is acceptable because runs are rare. Resolution reconciles judge + user: width is governed by the floor while work remains; total spend is governed by budget. Budget exhaustion stops launching NEW agents (run winds down) rather than throttling live concurrency below 20. This satisfies COST_CONTROL_BUDGET_DEPTH (bounds totals) without violating the user's floor (bounds width).
alternatives_considered: Unconditional floor of 20 with no budget bound at all (rejected: runaway cost, no governor)
Let budget/rate-limits dynamically lower the live floor below 20 (rejected: violates explicit user hard requirement)
Static min(cores-2,N) cap (rejected: user override)
decisions.risk: Subscription concurrency on Claude CLI may not sustain ~10 simultaneous claude processes; 20 parallel LLM CLIs may hit OOM/rate limits. Mitigated by Claude/Codex 50/50 balancing, refill-queue, 429 backoff/rebalance, and an empirical pre-flight concurrency probe.
decisions.test: Stress run with >20 jobs: live PID sampling shows 20+ active agent processes simultaneously (not merely queued), and the run still terminates within the configured total-agent/token budget.

decisions.decision: PROVE_REAL_PARALLELISM — Sample live audit-agent PIDs, record peak_concurrency and a concurrency timeline in the audit report, asserting peak>=20 when sufficient work exists.
decisions.rationale: A,B; judge 0.79, highest specificity. Silent sequential execution is a known failure mode here; PID-level telemetry is the only credible proof the fan-out is genuinely concurrent rather than serialized. Strong regression protection.
alternatives_considered: Trust dispatch logs / start-timestamps as proof of concurrency
No explicit parallelism telemetry
decisions.risk: PID sampling cadence could miss short-lived peaks. Mitigated by sampling at sub-second/second granularity and reporting max observed plus timeline.
decisions.test: An audit report from a sufficiently-loaded test run contains a concurrency timeline and a peak_concurrency >= 20 metric.

decisions.decision: LLM_CLI_ONLY — All audit agents invoke ONLY Claude CLI and Codex CLI; no raw API, no Gemini. Mix models and reasoning/effort tiers for finder/verifier diversity.
decisions.rationale: A,C; judge 0.80; user constraint (msg 53853634) overrides earlier gemini note. Reuses the bridge's existing driver agent-invoke infra, avoids raw-API key management, and the two-provider split enables rate-limit failover. Diversity of models/effort improves perspective coverage.
alternatives_considered: Include Gemini-2.5-pro or other providers
Raw Anthropic/OpenAI API calls bypassing the CLIs
decisions.risk: Single-provider concurrency/usage limits if balance skews. Mitigated by RATE_LIMIT_HANDLING and provider balancing.
decisions.test: Audit invocation trace shows exclusively claude-code CLI and codex CLI process spawns; no raw-API or Gemini calls present.

decisions.decision: RATE_LIMIT_HANDLING — Provider-aware 429/usage-limit handling: detect from CLI output, exponential backoff + retry, ~50/50 Claude/Codex balancing, and re-distribute queued jobs to the less-throttled provider to keep the concurrency floor.
decisions.rationale: Unanimous (A,B,C), judge 0.78. With 20+ concurrent CLI agents this is the load-bearing resilience piece for the concurrency goal; without it the floor is unachievable. Detecting limits from CLI stderr/exit codes and rebalancing is non-trivial but the failure mode (cascading 429s collapsing the fan-out) is severe.
alternatives_considered: No rate-limit handling (fail the agent on 429)
Lower concurrency on 429 instead of rebalancing (rejected: violates floor)
decisions.risk: Mis-detection of 429 vs other CLI errors could mis-route. Mitigated by explicit provider-specific error signature matching and capped retry counts.
decisions.test: Inject simulated 429s from one provider; verify backoff+retry, job rebalancing to the other provider, and that the 20+ floor is sustained.

decisions.decision: ORCHESTRATION_PARALLELPS1_FIX — Fan out via driver agent-invoke + lib/parallel.ps1 using a NEW read-only subprocess harness (not the worktree/merge code path), fixing parallel-pipe instability, untracked-cleanup pathspec bug, and codex hang.
decisions.rationale: Unanimous (A,B,C), judge 0.77, high specificity. The audit is read-only, so the worktree/merge machinery (source of past instability) is unnecessary and risky — a read-only subprocess harness avoids the untracked-cleanup pathspec issue entirely. Naming the exact defects to fix and testing with wide-fanout dummy jobs is the right scope.
alternatives_considered: Reuse lib/parallel.ps1's worktree/merge functions as-is
Write a brand-new orchestrator outside lib/parallel.ps1
Use the operator's Workflow tool (not available in the bridge)
decisions.risk: Touching known-unstable code may surface new edge cases. Mitigated by isolating the new harness, regression tests, and dummy-job stress fixtures before live agent use.
decisions.test: Wide-fanout stress test (20–30 dummy CLI jobs) through the read-only harness: stable, correct per-job stdout/stderr capture, timeout handling, and no hangs.

decisions.decision: AGENT_FAULT_ISOLATION — Strict per-agent isolation: one agent's timeout/crash/empty-reply never aborts the phase; status, stderr, and artifacts are preserved; the orchestrator decides retry vs degraded quorum.
decisions.rationale: A,B; judge 0.84 (highest correctness/risk-reduction). Mandatory for any 20+-agent fan-out — partial failure must be the norm, not a fatal event. Preserving artifacts and allowing degraded quorum keeps the audit useful even with casualties.
alternatives_considered: Fail the whole phase on any agent error
Silently drop failed agents without recording artifacts
decisions.risk: Degraded quorum could weaken verify confidence if too many skeptics die. Mitigated by recording quorum size per finding and flagging low-confidence verifications in the report.
decisions.test: Inject controlled per-agent failures (timeout, crash, malformed output) in a multi-agent run; the overall audit completes, failures are logged, artifacts preserved, and quorum decisions are recorded.

decisions.decision: COST_CONTROL_BUDGET_DEPTH — Budget profile enforcing total-agent caps, token budgets, configurable depth (#dimensions, verifiers-per-finding, finder rounds), a pre-flight cost estimate, and VERIFY early-exit when FIND returns zero findings.
decisions.rationale: Unanimous (A,B,C), judge 0.82. The principled governor against runaway cost on a deliberately-expensive run. Per the conflict resolution, these bounds cap the RUN's total size and spend (not its live width) — budget exhaustion winds the run down by ceasing new launches. The zero-findings early-exit avoids paying for an empty VERIFY phase.
alternatives_considered: No budget governor (rely on rarity of runs)
Use budget to throttle live concurrency below the 20 floor (rejected: violates user hard requirement)
decisions.risk: Aggressive caps could truncate a legitimately large finding set. Mitigated by milestone-tier budget profiles and explicit logging of any truncation/skipped work (no silent caps).
decisions.test: Configure a budget profile with agent cap, token ceiling, and depth knobs; verify the run respects them, logs any truncation, and early-exits VERIFY when FIND yields zero findings.

decisions.decision: PROJECT_MAP_PLAN_FIRST — Produce a PROJECT_MAP+PLAN (entrypoints, deep-audit/deep-LLM layer, driver agent-invoke, lib/parallel.ps1, backlog writer, scheduler hooks, concurrency model, cost control, two modes, parallelism proof) for architect review and user approval BEFORE any code.
decisions.rationale: A,C; judge 0.855 (highest total). Cheap, high-reversibility insurance against building the wrong thing given the high-cost/low-reversibility architecture atoms downstream. The task contract is DISCUSS-first and explicitly forbids building before approval.
alternatives_considered: Start implementation incrementally and document as we go
Skip the formal plan since the architecture is 'proven'
decisions.risk: Plan could under-specify the concurrency/rate-limit mechanics. Mitigated by requiring the plan to explicitly answer: how 20+ is held on Claude+Codex CLIs, OOM/rate-limit handling, and how parallelism is proven.
decisions.test: A comprehensive PROJECT_MAP+PLAN exists, is architect-reviewed, and is formally user-approved before any implementation commit.

decisions.decision: FIND_CONFIGURABLE_DIMENSIONS — FIND accepts a configurable dimension list (default for code: correctness, security, concurrency, error-handling, resources, contracts) and launches all finder jobs simultaneously.
decisions.rationale: A,C; judge 0.81. The dimension list is the unit of parallelism that justifies the concurrency floor and is target-tunable. Simultaneous launch (not round-robin) is the user's explicit concurrency requirement for the FIND phase.
alternatives_considered: Hardcoded fixed dimension set
Sequential per-dimension finder launches
decisions.risk: Too many dimensions could blow the budget. Mitigated by depth config in COST_CONTROL_BUDGET_DEPTH bounding dimension count.
decisions.test: Configure a custom dimension list; verify a finder agent is spawned per dimension and all run concurrently (visible in the concurrency timeline).

decisions.decision: FIND_STRUCTURED_JSON_OUTPUT — Each finder returns ONLY structured JSON conforming to a schema (root_cause, file, line, evidence_snippet, severity, why, fix_sketch, confidence); malformed output is rejected or repaired.
decisions.rationale: A,C; judge 0.82, very high specificity. An enumerated schema is required for downstream dedup/verify/synthesize to be machine-driven rather than prose-parsed. Confidence + evidence_snippet feed the adversarial verify stage.
alternatives_considered: Free-form prose findings parsed heuristically
Loosely-typed output without a strict schema
decisions.risk: CLIs may emit non-JSON or wrapped JSON. Mitigated by a parse/repair step and rejecting unrepairable output (logged, not silently dropped).
decisions.test: Run a finder; validate output against the schema; confirm malformed output is rejected or repaired and the event is logged.

decisions.decision: VERIFY_ADVERSARIAL_MAJORITY_REFUTE — VERIFY is adversarial: each finding is false-by-default; all skeptics for all findings spawn simultaneously; each skeptic must cite current file:line evidence to refute; majority-refute discards the finding; refuted findings are retained in the report.
decisions.rationale: A,B; judge 0.79. This is the adversarial core that turns a finder dump into a trustworthy report and is the main defense against false positives — it is the source of 'power'. Simultaneous skeptic launch satisfies the user's verify-phase concurrency requirement. Retaining refuted findings provides transparency/auditability.
alternatives_considered: Single-verifier-per-finding (no quorum)
Confirm-by-default verification
Sequential skeptic launch
Drop refuted findings entirely from the report
decisions.risk: High agent count and voting cost; degraded quorum from agent failures could weaken verdicts. Mitigated by AGENT_FAULT_ISOLATION quorum tracking and recording skeptic vote counts per finding.
decisions.test: Feed a mix of true and false findings; verify skeptics spawn concurrently, refute/confirm by majority with mandatory file:line citation, and refuted findings appear (marked) in the report.

decisions.decision: SYNTHESIZE_DEDUP_RANK_AUTOTASK — Dedup confirmed findings, rank by severity, and auto-create structured backlog fix-tasks (critical/high) with an idempotency key preventing duplicate tasks across runs.
decisions.rationale: A,B; judge 0.82. Closes the audit loop into the existing backlog writer — directly addressing the recently-fixed 'findings never transition' gap (see commit 0204426). The idempotency key is the critical detail preventing duplicate-task spam across repeated milestone runs.
alternatives_considered: Emit a report only, no auto-tasking
Auto-task without an idempotency key (rejected: duplicate spam across runs)
Auto-task every severity including low/info
decisions.risk: Idempotency key collisions or drift (e.g., line numbers shift) could mis-dedup. Mitigated by a content/root-cause-based key rather than raw line numbers, plus dedup-on-write in the backlog writer.
decisions.test: Run SYNTHESIZE with confirmed findings; verify backlog tasks are created with correct severity ranking and metadata, and a re-run with the same findings creates no duplicates.

decisions.decision: THIN_PROMPTS_FAT_TOOLS — Finder/verifier agents get thin prompts (dimension + location) and fat tools; the CLI reads code itself (codex -s read-only; claude -p --allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob --add-dir) instead of stdin-stuffing large context.
decisions.rationale: Single-proposal (B) but judge 0.83 and well-aligned with LLM_CLI_ONLY. Letting the CLI read live files avoids token-heavy stdin context-stuffing, cuts cost, prevents stale-snapshot risk, and simplifies the orchestrator's plumbing. Concrete flags provided.
alternatives_considered: Pre-stuff full file/code context into agent stdin
Provide a curated context bundle per agent
decisions.risk: Agents could wander beyond intended scope or read too broadly, inflating tokens. Mitigated by scoping --add-dir / read-only roots and passing a precise location hint per dimension.
decisions.test: Verify agent prompts are concise and invocation uses read-only CLI flags enabling direct filesystem reads, with no large code snippets passed via stdin.

rejected.decision: Use Gemini (e.g. gemini-2.5-pro) or raw provider APIs for audit agents.
rejected.why: User constraint (msg 53853634) overrides the earlier gemini note: ONLY Claude CLI + Codex CLI, never raw API, never Gemini. Reuses bridge driver agent-invoke infra and avoids API-key management. (See LLM_CLI_ONLY.)

rejected.decision: An unconditional hard floor of 20 concurrent agents with no budget bound, OR letting budget/rate-limits dynamically lower live concurrency below 20.
rejected.why: Both extremes rejected by the conflict resolution. Unbounded floor risks runaway cost (judge penalty on CONCURRENCY_FLOOR_20PLUS); lowering below 20 violates the user's explicit hard requirement. Resolution: floor governs live width while work remains; budget bounds total run size/spend and winds the run down by ceasing new launches, not by throttling width.

rejected.decision: Trigger the adversarial deep audit on the nightly cron.
rejected.why: Effectiveness>cost only holds because runs are RARE. Nightly deep runs would be prohibitively expensive and the user requires milestone/on-demand triggering with the cheap static audit retained as the nightly guard. (See AUDIT_MODES_SEPARATION.)

rejected.decision: Use lib/parallel.ps1's worktree/merge code path for audit fan-out.
rejected.why: The audit is read-only — worktree creation/merge is unnecessary and is the source of past instability (untracked-cleanup pathspec). A read-only subprocess harness is simpler and avoids that failure mode. (See ORCHESTRATION_PARALLELPS1_FIX.)

rejected.decision: Keep the single-pass finder dump without an adversarial VERIFY stage.
rejected.why: That is essentially the current weak design (one pass, no re-check). The adversarial majority-refute verify is the core source of 'power' — it filters false positives and confirms real bugs. (See VERIFY_ADVERSARIAL_MAJORITY_REFUTE.)

rejected.decision: Pre-stuff full code context into agent stdin.
rejected.why: Inflates tokens, risks stale snapshots, and complicates plumbing. Thin prompts + fat tools (CLI reads live files read-only) is cheaper and fresher. (See THIN_PROMPTS_FAT_TOOLS.)

rejected.decision: Repair the existing deep:deep_failed subprocess/job layer in place rather than replacing it.
rejected.why: It is historically broken and architecturally a single un-verified pass. Replacing it with the proven three-phase orchestrator is higher-impact than patching. (See ARCH_3PHASE_REPLACE_DEEPLLM.)

next_step: Author the PROJECT_MAP+PLAN document (Phase 0) — explicitly specifying the concurrency model and how >=20 simultaneous Claude+Codex CLI agents are held under the budget-bounds-total / floor-bounds-width resolution, the rate-limit/OOM strategy, and the PID-based parallelism proof — then submit it for architect review and user approval before writing any code.

red_team_findings.what: The decision reinterprets the user's HARD ≥20 concurrency floor as a 'conditional target bounded by the budget ceiling,' explicitly allowing concurrency to drop below 20 when 'budget is genuinely insufficient.' The user pre-adjudicated exactly this conflict: 'НЕ опускать одновременность ниже 20' / 'не меньше' (msg 53853633) and 'Стоимость/нагрузка высокая — ОК т.к. редкий milestone-запуск' — i.e. provision budget high enough and never drop below 20; handle limits via refill-queue-to-floor + retries, not by lowering concurrency.
red_team_findings.why: The work-conditional relaxation ('при достаточном объёме') IS user-sanctioned, but the budget-conditional relaxation below 20 directly contradicts an explicit, repeated, emphatic hard requirement. The user's resolution was 'set agent-cap ≥20', not 'let budget win and go below 20'. Worse, a DISCUSS-first task requires user approval to weaken a stated requirement; the record bakes in the weakening as a settled 'modify (0.695)' decision instead of surfacing it as an open question for the user to re-confirm.

red_team_findings.what: No code snapshot / git-SHA pin for the audit. 20+ finder and skeptic agents read the LIVE working tree of a repo that auto-commits during normal operation (git log shows '[task:...] auto-commit (driver...)' commits). The decision rejects worktrees on the grounds that 'a read-only audit performs no file mutations or merges' — conflating 'no merge needed' with 'no snapshot needed.'
red_team_findings.why: Over a long (~1.5M-token) multi-agent run, the tree can change under the agents: finders read one state, skeptics read another → VERIFY's mandatory 'current file:line' check wrongly refutes real findings or confirms stale ones, and SYNTHESIZE line-drift/idempotency problems compound. The core adversarial value-add depends on all agents seeing identical code. A read-only worktree pinned to a fixed SHA would solve consistency (and write-isolation) — the blanket worktree rejection threw out snapshot isolation along with merge machinery. The 'bounded by the milestone (frozen) trigger' assumption has no actual freeze/pin mechanism behind it.

red_team_findings.what: The FIND phase cannot meet the ≥20 concurrency floor as designed. The FIND decision states 'an agent is spawned per dimension' with its test 'verify an agent is spawned per dimension,' and the default dimension list is ~6 (correctness/security/concurrency/error-handling/resources/contracts). 6 dimensions → ~6 concurrent finders, not 20.
red_team_findings.why: The user requires ≥20 concurrent in BOTH phases (success_test: 'During both the FIND and VERIFY phases ... minimum of 20 concurrent agents'). FIND volume is the small, configured dimension count — not unbounded work — so the 'sufficient volume' escape hatch hides a structural shortfall. The decision never reconciles 1-agent-per-dimension with ≥20: it would need multiple model/reasoning profiles per dimension (e.g. ~3-4 finders/angle) or ~20 dimensions, neither of which is specified. As written, the FIND-phase floor success_test fails.

red_team_findings.what: 'Replace deep:deep_failed removes the root failure surface' is asserted, not established. In the code, deep_failed is not one bug — it is a catch-all status set at numerous independent points (audit.ps1:1296,1323,1355,1362,1372; aggregated 1957-1962) covering subprocess launch, JSON parse, and job-layer failures. The new system rebuilds on the same subprocess/CLI/JSON-parse layer (and the same codex-restricted-user sandbox, parallel.ps1:95,375-389, where the codex-hang/pathspec issues actually live).
red_team_findings.why: Without diagnosing WHICH failure point actually fires in production, 'replace' may re-inherit the identical subprocess/parse fragility under a new name. The codex hang and untracked-cleanup pathspec issues are tied to codex's restricted-user sandbox and git-metadata writes, not solely to worktree/merge — so the 'read-only harness avoids the instability' claim is not proven. The implementation plan fixes three NAMED instabilities but contains no 'root-cause deep_failed' step, so success_test ('deep-LLM part successfully fixed') is at risk.

red_team_findings.what: The existing deep path ALREADY auto-files unverified codex/claude findings directly to the backlog (Add-Idea at audit.ps1:1489,1522) with no adversarial verification. The decision adds VERIFY-before-file but relies on 'replace the old path'; it does not call out removing this existing direct-file code.
red_team_findings.why: If replacement is partial (a real risk given deep_failed touches many sites), the OLD unverified Add-Idea path keeps firing — so the system either double-files (old unverified + new verified) or the unverified false-positive spam the VERIFY gate exists to stop continues to reach the backlog, silently defeating the core value-add. The removal must be explicit and tested, not implied.

red_team_findings.what: The VERIFY quorum rule is logically inconsistent. It states findings are 'false-by-default until proven by current file:line' (a CONFIRM-threshold rule) AND 'discarded on majority-refute' (a KEEP-unless-majority-refutes rule). These are different decision functions with opposite defaults.
red_team_findings.why: For a split skeptic vote (e.g. 1 refute / 1 confirm / 1 abstain, or all skeptics silent), the survival condition is undefined. 'False by default' implies the finding dies unless a majority affirmatively confirms the file:line holds; 'discard on majority-refute' implies it survives unless a majority refutes. Combined with the degraded-quorum 'minimum valid skeptic count' (still open), a true bug can be silently dropped or a false positive silently kept depending on which rule the implementer codes. Needs a single crisp confirm/refute threshold.

red_team_findings.what: Behavior when FIND yields many findings and VERIFY (findings × skeptics) exceeds the budget cap is undefined. With, say, 100 findings × 3 skeptics = 300 agents, the hard budget ceiling truncates VERIFY, but the decision never says what happens to the unverified remainder.
red_team_findings.why: Two bad outcomes, both unaddressed: (a) drop unverified findings → real critical bugs are silently lost (false negatives — the opposite of the audit's purpose), or (b) file them unverified → they bypass the adversarial gate that is the system's entire reason to exist. The FIND-zero early-exit is handled; the FIND-flood case (more dangerous) is not. A deterministic policy (severity-prioritized verification within budget, plus explicit logging of unverified findings) is required.

red_team_findings.what: The backlog idempotency key is composed from 'root_cause + file + normalized line,' where root_cause is free-text generated by an LLM.
red_team_findings.why: LLM-generated root_cause phrasing is non-deterministic across runs (same bug, different wording) and the code itself drifts between milestone runs. This makes the key unstable in both directions: the same real bug described differently → duplicate backlog tasks (the exact spam the key is meant to prevent), while a genuinely new bug with similar wording near the same line → wrongly suppressed. Keying on volatile LLM prose cannot reliably deduplicate; a stable structural key (e.g. file + symbol/normalized-snippet hash, not prose) is needed.

red_team_findings.what: 'Pragmatic reuse of lib/parallel.ps1' materially understates effort and risk. The module is wholly built around git worktrees + sequential merge and a fire-ALL-workers-at-once dispatch with no concurrency cap, no refill queue, and no read-only path (parallel.ps1:1,18). Reusable surface is essentially just the worker-registry config (parallel.workers); the read-only subprocess harness, the refill-queue worker pool, maxStreams capping, and PID telemetry are all net-new.
red_team_findings.why: The decision's risk framing ('reuse existing dispatch, less surface') is inverted — almost none of the dispatch core is reusable for a read-only, pooled, capped fan-out. 'maxStreams' does not even appear in parallel.ps1 today, and the current 'launch every worker in parallel' with no cap is itself a likely cause of the 'parallel-pipe instability' under wide fan-out. Building a managed pool is a from-scratch orchestrator alongside (not on top of) the existing one, raising the build cost the plan budgets for and the chance the named-instability fixes miss the real blocker.

red_team_findings.what: The parallelism proof (sampling live agent PIDs for peak_concurrency ≥ 20) does not define WHAT counts as an agent process. Claude CLI and Codex CLI each spawn child processes (node, sandbox helpers), and the bridge driver may itself be a CLI process.
red_team_findings.why: Naive PID counting over-counts (each agent's child node/helper processes inflate the number, so 8 real agents can read as 20+) or under-counts (sampling the wrong process layer). The decision flags sampling cadence/skew but not process-identity, so the headline 'peak ≥ 20' assertion — the very evidence meant to defeat fake/sequential parallelism — can be satisfied without 20 real concurrent agents. The sampler needs an explicit agent-process identity rule (tagged PIDs / process-group roots), not just a cadence.
